(8) Review independence: [family is the model family of the run, not the harness: a dsh run on a DeepSeek model is family deepseek and cannot be reviewed by lan-deepseek-*]. (9) Ship ddflow as a dsh bundle package: [defer; overlay first]. chunk_findings.detail: `"matcher": "*"` is not a valid Claude Code/dsh hook matcher: Claude Code bridge matcher values are regexes, and `*` has no preceding atom, so it either fails config validation or never matches. chunk_findings.title: tests/fixtures/dsh_probe/hooks_example.json:3-4

chunk_findings.detail: The file is named and intended as an MCP handshake fixture, but the first client message uses `method: "server/discover"` and nests `protocolVersion`/`clientInfo`/`clientCapabilities` under `params._meta`. MCP handshake requires an `initialize` request with those values at the params level, followed by an `initialize` response; this file contains neither. Given a standard MCP server or MCP-validating consumer, line 1 returns a JSON-RPC `Method not found` error, so the subsequent `tools/list` and `tools/call` exchanges in lines 3-6 would never occur.
chunk_findings.title: tests/fixtures/dsh_probe/mcp_handshake.ndjson:1

chunk_findings.detail: The `tools/list` response (`s2c`, id 0) returns `{"tools_count":123, "tool_names":[ ... ], "tools_json_chars":109750}` and omits the required `tools` array. MCP `tools/list` results must contain a `tools` array of tool definitions; a compliant client or test consuming this line gets no tools or a validation error, so the fixture cannot establish “whether tools appear before the first turn” as the probe intends.
chunk_findings.title: tests/fixtures/dsh_probe/mcp_handshake.ndjson:4

chunk_findings.detail: The committed fixture leaves literal `<SCRATCH>` placeholders in the MCP client `args` (line 24), `cwd` (line 25), hook module path (line 27), `configPath` (line 29), and `projectDir` (line 30). chunk_findings.detail: `cordis_rows` overwrites duplicate marker names (last line wins), and `_cordis_place` replaces only the first `# ddflow-row:<name>` occurrence. chunk_findings.detail: The dsh descriptor omits `budget = 65536` even though the change intent explicitly specifies `[instructions] ... budget 65536 bytes`. If harness loaders consume `instructions.budget` to cap how much of AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md is read, dsh will not have the declared 65536-byte budget; depending on validation this either fails descriptor loading or silently falls back to a different default, so instruction files can be truncated at the wrong size for dsh.

chunk_findings.detail: The hook event map lists only `SessionStart`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, and `Stop`, but the change intent says the hooks-claude-code bridge also emits `SubagentStart` and `SubagentStop`. For a dsh session that spawns a subagent (dsh has native subagent tools), the generated `.ddflow/harness/dsh.hooks.json` will not register those two events, so ddflow never receives subagent start/stop hooks and any policy attached to subagent lifecycle is silently skipped. The descriptor should include `subagent_start = "SubagentStart"` and `subagent_stop = "SubagentStop"`.

Given a run that spawns a subagent, a generated hooks configuration following this delta would not expect or handle the `SubagentStart`/`SubagentStop` events that dsh actually emits, so session/prompt injection or other hook behavior intended for subagents would be missing or misregistered.
